issue.standard_remedy: Route off-contract buying to contracted suppliers
issue.summary: 64% of category spend is off contract

plan.diagnosis: 64% of Rubber compounds category spend (USD 6,415,649 out of USD 10,075,096 total) is occurring off-contract across 9 plants, representing high-severity maverick spend in a direct material category. This indicates lack of source list enforcement, decentralized purchasing behaviors, and failure to leverage contracted supplier agreements, resulting in lost volume discounts and compliance erosion.

remedy_steps.step: Immediately audit all Rubber compounds POs across SAP, Oracle EBS, Dynamics 365, and NetSuite for the trailing 12 months to identify non-contracted suppliers and requester patterns by plant

Implement source list restrictions in all ERPs: activate source list enforcement for Rubber compounds category, limit approved vendors to contracted suppliers only, and communicate new policy to all 9 plant procurement teams
remedy_steps.owner: ERP System Administrator & Category Manager - Rubber compounds

remedy_steps.step: Negotiate volume consolidation rebates with contracted Rubber compounds suppliers based on redirecting USD 6.4M maverick spend, targeting 5-8% price reduction on total category spend
Configure Coupa to route all Rubber compounds requisitions through mandatory catalog punch-out to contracted suppliers, with approval workflow escalation for any non-catalog requests
Conduct training sessions for requesters and buyers at all 9 plants on contracted supplier usage, source list compliance requirements, and penalty enforcement for policy violations
Establish monthly compliance dashboards tracking on-contract spend percentage by plant, with escalation to Plant Managers for sites below 90% compliance

plan.expected_impact: Redirecting USD 6,415,649 maverick spend to contracted suppliers and negotiating volume-based pricing is expected to deliver USD 320,000 to USD 500,000 in annual savings (5-8% of maverick spend).
kpis: On-contract spend percentage for Rubber compounds (target: >95% within 6 months)
Maverick spend value reduction (target: reduce USD 6,415,649 to <USD 500,000)
Number of active Rubber compounds suppliers (target: consolidate to contracted vendors only)
Average purchase price variance vs. contracted rates (target: 0% premium)
Compliance rate by plant (target: all 9 plants >90%)
risks: Plant resistance due to established relationships with non-contracted suppliers or perceived quality/delivery advantages
Supply disruption if contracted suppliers cannot absorb full USD 10M volume across 9 plant locations
ERP source list enforcement gaps if master data (material-plant combinations) is incomplete across SAP, Oracle, Dynamics, NetSuite
Contracted supplier capacity constraints leading to requesters seeking non-catalog emergency purchases
Delayed ERP configuration rollout across multi-system environment causing compliance monitoring blind spots
erp_actions: SAP: Activate source list requirement (ME01) for all Rubber compounds materials, set indicator '1' (source list required) in material master (MARC-KORDB), apply vendor posting blocks (XK05) to non-contracted suppliers for Rubber compounds purchasing org

Oracle EBS: Create and enforce Approved Supplier List (ASL) entries for Rubber compounds category items, set 'Use only Approved Suppliers' flag in purchasing options, disable non-contracted vendors for category
Dynamics 365: Configure Trade Agreements for contracted Rubber compounds suppliers with price/discount schedules, enable 'Approved vendor check' policy rules in procurement parameters
NetSuite: Build and assign Preferred Vendor records for all Rubber compounds items, set 'Restrict to Preferred Vendors' on item records, create saved searches to flag non-contracted POs
Coupa: Map contracted Rubber compounds suppliers to catalogs, enable 'Preferred Supplier' routing rules, configure approval workflows requiring VP sign-off for non-catalog requests >USD 5,000

All ERPs: Create custom compliance reports/dashboards showing on-contract vs. off-contract spend by plant, material, and supplier; schedule weekly automated distribution to category managers and plant leads
